hook.line: At the hearing, Tomás gets three minutes. A good speaker says what they'll argue and how many reasons they have, so the room can follow.
hook.es: Voy a defender que el café debe quedarse, por dos razones.
hook.en: I am going to argue that the café should stay, for two reasons.

examples.es: Voy a defender que el barrio debe tener más parques, por tres razones.
examples.en: I am going to argue that the neighbourhood should have more parks, for three reasons.

rule:
To open an argument, say your position and promise your structure.

*Voy a defender que* + your claim. It means *I am going to argue that*, and *que* starts a normal sentence: *Voy a defender que el café debe quedarse.*
Then count: *por dos razones*, *por tres razones*, *por varias razones*.
Then deliver them in order: *En primer lugar,* ... then *en segundo lugar,* ...

For several people, *vamos a defender que*.

English says *argue*, but Spanish *defender* is also *defend*. Use it when you stand behind a position.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the thesis statement and signposting of an argumentative speech.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *dos* or *tres*, then type the whole sentence: Voy a defender que el café debe quedarse, por ___ razones. (for three reasons)

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I am going to argue that the café should stay in La Candelaria.
yourTurn.answer: Voy a defender que el café debe quedarse en La Candelaria.

yourTurn.answer: En primer lugar, es parte del patrimonio del barrio.

yourTurn.why: We is *vamos*, and the claim is a normal sentence.

pitfalls.wrong: Voy a defender el barrio debe tener más parques.
pitfalls.right: Voy a defender que el barrio debe tener más parques.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English can say *argue the centre should*, but Spanish needs *que* to start the claim.

pitfalls.wrong: Voy a defender que el barrio debe tener más parques, para tres razones.
pitfalls.right: Voy a defender que el barrio debe tener más parques, por tres razones.
En primer lugar, hay menos contaminación.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase is *en primer lugar*, with *en*.
